# Peripheral Access Crate (PAC)

**Layer 2** of the embedded-Rust four-layer crate stack. A thin, **auto-generated** Rust wrapper over the [[MemoryMappedIO|memory-mapped registers]] of a specific microcontroller part number. Generated by [[Svd2Rust|`svd2rust`]] from the chip vendor's [[SVDFile|CMSIS-SVD XML file]] ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).

Examples: [[Tm4c123xCrate|`tm4c123x`]] (Texas Instruments Tiva-C TM4C123 series), `stm32f30x` (ST-Micro STM32F30x family — covering the [[STM32F303VCT6]]).

## The svd2rust closure API

A PAC exposes three primitives per register, all closure-based ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]):

- **`reg.read()`** — returns an `R` struct with typed read-only sub-field accessors. `pwm.ctl.read().globalsync0().is_set()`.
- **`reg.write(|w| …)`** — closure on a `W` struct; **resets all unset sub-fields to defaults** (existing register content is lost).
- **`reg.modify(|r, w| …)`** — two-argument closure (read + write); the safe replacement for C's read-modify-write pattern. Eliminates the wrong-variable footgun.

Sub-field accessors are marked `unsafe` when the [[SVDFile|SVD file]] does not enumerate valid values for the field — e.g. `unsafe { w.load().bits(263) }`.

## Stack position

- **Below**: [[MicroArchitectureCrate|micro-arch crate]] (core-level, e.g. [[CortexMCrate|`cortex-m`]]).
- **Above**: [[HALCrate|HAL crate]] (ergonomic portable layer); [[BoardCrate|board crate]] (dev-board-specific).

`Peripherals::take()` is the singleton gate — guarantees only one PAC `Peripherals` struct exists in the program ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).

## Connections

- [[Svd2Rust]] — the generator producing every PAC.
- [[SVDFile]] — the input format.
- [[MemoryMappedIO]] — the underlying hardware contract being wrapped.
- [[MicroArchitectureCrate]] — sits below in the stack.
- [[HALCrate]] — sits above.
- [[Tm4c123xCrate]] — the chapter's worked PAC example.
- [[CortexMRTCrate]] — provides the `#[entry]` runtime that wraps PAC code.
